description: Run a complete scientific investigation from literature search through hypothesis, experimental design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, and manuscript draft.

steps.description: Conduct a structured literature search across databases, filter by relevance and recency, extract key findings, and identify gaps in current knowledge.

inputs.name: research-topic
inputs.desc: The subject area or question to investigate

inputs.name: scope-constraints
inputs.desc: Date range, language, and database preferences

outputs.name: source-list
outputs.desc: Ranked list of relevant papers with citation data

outputs.name: knowledge-gap-summary
outputs.desc: Identified gaps and open questions in existing work

outputs.name: key-findings-digest
outputs.desc: Condensed summary of established results

process: Define search terms and Boolean operators from the research topic
Query target databases and collect candidate papers
Screen titles and abstracts against inclusion criteria
Extract key findings, methods, and conclusions from included papers
Synthesize gaps between what is known and what remains unanswered

steps.description: Convert knowledge gaps into one or more testable hypotheses with clearly defined independent and dependent variables.

inputs.name: knowledge-gap-summary
inputs.desc: Identified gaps from the literature search

outputs.name: hypothesis-statement
outputs.desc: Formal testable hypothesis with null and alternative forms

outputs.name: variable-definitions
outputs.desc: Independent, dependent, and controlled variables with measurement criteria

outputs.name: prediction-set
outputs.desc: Specific measurable predictions that follow from the hypothesis

process: Identify the most promising knowledge gap as the focal question
State the null and alternative hypotheses in falsifiable terms
Define each variable and its operational measurement
List predictions that distinguish the hypothesis from alternatives

steps.description: Design an experiment with appropriate controls, treatment groups, sample size justification, and a randomization scheme.

outputs.name: experiment-protocol
outputs.desc: Step-by-step procedure with controls, treatments, and timing

outputs.name: sample-size-justification
outputs.desc: Power analysis or precedent-based sample size rationale

outputs.name: randomization-plan
outputs.desc: Assignment method for subjects or samples to conditions

process: Choose the experimental design type (between, within, factorial, crossover)
Define treatment groups, controls, and replication count
Calculate or justify sample size from effect size and power requirements
Specify randomization and blinding procedures
Write the step-by-step protocol with timing and decision points

steps.description: Build a data collection plan with instrument specifications, recording formats, quality checks, and a schedule.

inputs.name: experiment-protocol
inputs.desc: The experimental procedure to collect data for

inputs.name: variable-definitions
inputs.desc: What needs to be measured and how

outputs.name: collection-plan
outputs.desc: Instrument list, recording format, schedule, and chain-of-custody rules

outputs.name: quality-check-criteria
outputs.desc: Acceptance thresholds, outlier rules, and calibration schedule

outputs.name: raw-data-schema
outputs.desc: Column definitions, units, and expected ranges for the dataset

process: List every measurement and match it to an instrument or method
Define the recording format, units, precision, and storage location
Set calibration intervals and quality acceptance thresholds
Build the collection schedule aligned to the experiment timeline

steps.description: Select appropriate statistical tests, define significance thresholds, plan for multiple comparisons, and specify the analysis pipeline before data are collected.

inputs.name: raw-data-schema
inputs.desc: Structure of the data to be analyzed

outputs.name: analysis-plan
outputs.desc: Ordered list of tests, assumptions, corrections, and decision criteria

outputs.name: significance-thresholds
outputs.desc: Alpha levels, correction method, and effect size benchmarks

process: Match each prediction to a statistical test based on data type and design
State assumptions (normality, independence, equal variance) and how to check them
Define alpha level and correction for multiple comparisons
Specify the analysis code or software and version to be used
Document stopping rules and interim analysis criteria if applicable

steps.description: Interpret statistical output in terms of the original hypothesis, assess effect sizes, identify unexpected patterns, and state what the data do and do not support.

inputs.name: significance-thresholds
inputs.desc: Decision criteria for acceptance or rejection

inputs.name: prediction-set
inputs.desc: What was predicted under the hypothesis

outputs.name: results-narrative
outputs.desc: Plain-language interpretation of each test outcome

outputs.name: effect-size-table
outputs.desc: Observed effect sizes with confidence intervals

outputs.name: limitations-list
outputs.desc: Caveats, confounds, and generalizability boundaries

process: Run each pre-registered test and record the output
Compare observed results against each prediction
Calculate and report effect sizes with confidence intervals
Identify patterns not predicted by the hypothesis
List limitations, confounds, and threats to validity

steps.description: Structure a scientific manuscript with standard sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion), integrate figures and tables, and format citations.

outputs.name: manuscript-draft
outputs.desc: Structured draft with all standard sections

outputs.name: figure-table-list
outputs.desc: Descriptions and captions for each figure and table

outputs.name: citation-list
outputs.desc: Formatted bibliography

process: Write the introduction from the literature context and knowledge gap
Describe methods in sufficient detail for replication
Present results with tables and figure placeholders
Write the discussion linking results to the hypothesis and prior work
Compile and format the reference list

description: Plan and execute a chemical synthesis from target molecule analysis through retrosynthetic planning, reaction optimization, analytical characterization, and purity assessment.

steps.description: Analyze a target molecule's structure, functional groups, stereochemistry, and known synthetic routes from the literature.

inputs.name: target-structure
inputs.desc: SMILES, InChI, or drawn structure of the target molecule

inputs.name: target-properties
inputs.desc: Desired purity, quantity, and any stereochemical requirements

outputs.name: functional-group-map
outputs.desc: Annotated list of functional groups, reactive sites, and protecting group needs

outputs.name: known-routes-summary
outputs.desc: Existing synthetic routes with yields and conditions from published work

outputs.name: stereochemistry-constraints
outputs.desc: Chiral centers, required configurations, and racemization risks

process: Parse the target structure and enumerate functional groups
Search databases (SciFinder, Reaxys) for known synthetic routes
Identify stereocenters and evaluate configuration control requirements
Flag protecting group needs for sensitive functional groups

steps.description: Decompose the target molecule into available starting materials through retrosynthetic disconnections, scoring each route by step count, yield estimate, and reagent availability.

inputs.name: functional-group-map
inputs.desc: Reactive sites and protecting group needs

outputs.name: retrosynthetic-tree
outputs.desc: Disconnection tree with scored candidate routes

outputs.name: selected-route
outputs.desc: Chosen route with starting materials and estimated step count

outputs.name: reagent-list
outputs.desc: All reagents, catalysts, and solvents required

process: Apply disconnection rules to identify strategic bonds
Generate candidate routes as a disconnection tree
Score each route on step count, predicted yield, and reagent cost
Select the best route and list all required reagents and solvents

steps.description: Optimize reaction conditions for each step: solvent, temperature, catalyst loading, reaction time, and workup procedure.

outputs.name: optimized-conditions
outputs.desc: Solvent, temperature, time, catalyst, and stoichiometry per step

outputs.name: workup-procedures
outputs.desc: Extraction, washing, and purification procedure per step

outputs.name: safety-notes
outputs.desc: Hazard flags, incompatibilities, and PPE requirements

process: Set baseline conditions from literature precedent for each reaction type
Identify variables to screen (solvent, temperature, catalyst, equivalents)
Design a small screening matrix for the most sensitive steps
Record optimized conditions and workup for each step
Flag hazardous reagents and incompatible combinations

steps.description: Plan analytical characterization for each intermediate and the final product using NMR, mass spectrometry, IR, and chromatography.

outputs.name: characterization-protocol
outputs.desc: Which techniques to run at each stage with expected diagnostic signals

outputs.name: expected-spectra
outputs.desc: Predicted NMR shifts, MS fragments, and IR bands for the target

outputs.name: purity-method
outputs.desc: HPLC or GC method for purity determination

process: List diagnostic signals (NMR chemical shifts, MS parent ion, IR bands) for the target
Assign characterization checkpoints at key intermediates
Define an HPLC or GC method for purity measurement
Specify acceptance criteria (purity threshold, spectral match tolerance)

steps.description: Calculate isolated yield, assess purity from chromatographic data, compare against predicted values, and identify loss points.

inputs.name: optimized-conditions
inputs.desc: The reaction conditions that were run

outputs.name: yield-report
outputs.desc: Isolated yield per step and overall, with mass balance

outputs.name: purity-report
outputs.desc: Measured purity with chromatogram references

outputs.name: loss-analysis
outputs.desc: Identified steps with yield loss and suggested improvements

process: Calculate isolated yield per step from mass recovered vs theoretical
Compute overall yield as the product of step yields
Report purity from chromatographic integration
Identify the highest-loss steps and propose improvements

description: Run a field biology investigation from species inventory through specimen collection, habitat assessment, DNA sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and biodiversity reporting.

steps.description: Design a species inventory method for a target area: define taxa of interest, choose survey methods (visual, trap, acoustic), and set sampling effort.

inputs.name: study-area
inputs.desc: Geographic location, coordinates, and habitat type

inputs.name: taxa-of-interest
inputs.desc: Which groups to survey (birds, insects, plants, etc.)

outputs.name: inventory-protocol
outputs.desc: Survey method, transect layout, trap types, and effort per session

outputs.name: species-checklist-template
outputs.desc: Recording form with expected species and identification keys

outputs.name: permits-needed
outputs.desc: Collection, access, or IACUC permits required

process: Review existing species records for the area
Select survey methods matched to each taxon (point counts, pitfall traps, quadrats, mist nets)
Design transect or plot layout for spatial coverage
Set sampling effort (sessions, duration, replicates) based on detection probability
Identify permitting requirements

steps.description: Plan specimen collection with preservation methods, labeling standards, chain of custody, and storage requirements.

inputs.name: inventory-protocol
inputs.desc: What will be collected and how

outputs.name: collection-protocol
outputs.desc: Collection methods, preservation, labeling, and storage per taxon

outputs.name: voucher-standards
outputs.desc: Voucher specimen preparation and museum deposition plan

outputs.name: field-kit-list
outputs.desc: Equipment, preservatives, and consumables needed

process: Match each taxon to an appropriate collection and preservation method
Define labeling fields (date, coordinates, collector, habitat notes)
Specify storage conditions and chain of custody
Plan voucher specimen preparation for museum deposition

steps.description: Assess habitat quality at the study site using vegetation structure, abiotic measurements, disturbance indicators, and land-use history.

inputs.name: species-checklist-template
inputs.desc: Species observed to contextualize habitat use

outputs.name: habitat-profile
outputs.desc: Vegetation structure, canopy cover, substrate, water features, and disturbance level

outputs.name: abiotic-measurements
outputs.desc: Temperature, humidity, pH, soil type, and water chemistry

outputs.name: disturbance-index
outputs.desc: Quantified disturbance level from land-use and physical indicators

process: Measure vegetation structure (canopy cover, understory density, tree DBH)
Record abiotic parameters at standardized points
Score disturbance from indicators (roads, clearings, invasive species, erosion)
Compile land-use history from maps and local records

steps.description: Extract DNA from field specimens, amplify target markers (COI, rbcL, ITS), prepare sequencing libraries, and run quality control on returned sequences.

inputs.name: collection-protocol
inputs.desc: Specimens available and preservation method used

inputs.name: taxa-of-interest
inputs.desc: Which markers to target per taxon

outputs.name: sequence-dataset
outputs.desc: Cleaned, trimmed sequences with specimen IDs and metadata

outputs.name: qc-report
outputs.desc: Read quality, alignment success rate, and contamination flags

outputs.name: marker-coverage-summary
outputs.desc: Which specimens yielded usable sequence for each marker

process: Extract DNA using a protocol matched to tissue type and preservative
Amplify target barcoding markers with appropriate primers
Prepare sequencing libraries and submit to sequencing facility
Trim, quality-filter, and align returned sequences
Flag contamination and low-quality reads

steps.description: Build a phylogenetic tree from sequence data: align sequences, select a substitution model, run tree inference, and assess branch support.

inputs.name: sequence-dataset
inputs.desc: Cleaned sequences from the sequencing workflow

outputs.name: phylogenetic-tree
outputs.desc: Best tree with branch support values

outputs.name: model-selection-log
outputs.desc: Substitution model comparison and chosen model

outputs.name: clade-summary
outputs.desc: Major clades, divergence patterns, and taxonomic implications

process: Perform multiple sequence alignment (MAFFT or MUSCLE)
Select the best substitution model using information criteria
Run maximum likelihood or Bayesian tree inference
Assess branch support via bootstrap or posterior probability
Annotate clades and compare to existing taxonomy

steps.description: Compile a biodiversity report with species richness, diversity indices, community composition, and conservation recommendations.

outputs.name: biodiversity-report
outputs.desc: Species richness, Shannon index, evenness, rarefaction curves, and community composition

outputs.name: conservation-flags
outputs.desc: Threatened species detected and habitat concerns

outputs.name: management-recommendations
outputs.desc: Actions to maintain or improve biodiversity at the site

process: Calculate species richness and abundance-based diversity indices
Build rarefaction and accumulation curves to assess sampling completeness
Describe community composition and compare to reference sites
Flag species of conservation concern from IUCN or regional lists
Write management recommendations based on habitat and species status

description: Design and analyze a physics experiment: identify the phenomenon, design the apparatus, build an uncertainty budget, calibrate instruments, plan data acquisition, fit models, and analyze systematic errors.

steps.description: Identify and scope the physical phenomenon to investigate, state the governing theory, and define what measurement would confirm or refute the prediction.

inputs.name: research-question
inputs.desc: The physical question or effect to investigate

inputs.name: theoretical-context
inputs.desc: Relevant equations, models, or predicted values

outputs.name: phenomenon-scope
outputs.desc: Defined effect with parameter ranges and predicted magnitude

outputs.name: measurable-quantities
outputs.desc: What to measure, expected values, and required precision

outputs.name: governing-equations
outputs.desc: Equations linking measured quantities to the phenomenon

process: State the physical effect and the theory that predicts it
Identify which quantities to measure and to what precision
Estimate the expected signal magnitude and noise floor
Define the criterion for a positive detection vs null result

steps.description: Design the measurement apparatus: select sensors, define geometry, specify materials, and draw the schematic with critical dimensions.

inputs.name: measurable-quantities
inputs.desc: What needs to be measured and precision required

outputs.name: apparatus-schematic
outputs.desc: Labeled diagram with sensor placement, geometry, and materials

outputs.name: sensor-specifications
outputs.desc: Each sensor's range, resolution, response time, and accuracy

outputs.name: critical-dimensions
outputs.desc: Tolerances on distances, alignments, and angles that affect the measurement

process: Select sensors that cover the required measurement range and precision
Define the physical layout and mounting geometry
Specify materials considering interference, thermal expansion, and vibration
Draw the schematic with critical dimensions and tolerances

steps.description: Build a complete uncertainty budget: identify every error source (statistical, systematic, environmental), estimate each contribution, and propagate to the final result.

inputs.name: governing-equations
inputs.desc: How measured quantities combine into the result

outputs.name: uncertainty-budget
outputs.desc: Table of error sources, type (A or B), magnitude, and contribution to combined uncertainty

outputs.name: dominant-error-sources
outputs.desc: Ranked list of the largest contributors to total uncertainty

outputs.name: combined-uncertainty
outputs.desc: Propagated combined standard uncertainty and expanded uncertainty

process: List every source of uncertainty (sensor, alignment, environment, model)
Classify each as Type A (statistical) or Type B (systematic)
Estimate the magnitude of each contribution
Propagate through the governing equations to the final combined uncertainty
Identify the dominant sources and whether they can be reduced

steps.description: Write a calibration protocol for each instrument: reference standards, procedure, acceptance criteria, and recalibration schedule.

inputs.name: dominant-error-sources
inputs.desc: Which calibrations matter most for accuracy

outputs.name: calibration-protocol
outputs.desc: Step-by-step calibration procedure per instrument with reference standards

outputs.name: acceptance-criteria
outputs.desc: Pass/fail thresholds and drift limits

outputs.name: calibration-schedule
outputs.desc: When to recalibrate during the experiment

process: Select a traceable reference standard for each instrument
Write the calibration procedure (apply known input, record response, fit)
Set acceptance thresholds based on the uncertainty budget allocation
Define recalibration triggers (time interval, temperature shift, physical disturbance)

steps.description: Plan the data acquisition: sampling rate, number of runs, recording format, real-time monitoring, and abort criteria.

inputs.name: uncertainty-budget
inputs.desc: Required measurement count for statistical power

outputs.name: acquisition-plan
outputs.desc: Sampling rates, channels, file format, run count, and storage estimate

outputs.name: monitoring-dashboard-spec
outputs.desc: Real-time quantities to display for operator decisions

outputs.name: abort-criteria
outputs.desc: Conditions that stop data taking (drift, saturation, anomaly)

process: Set sampling rate per channel based on signal bandwidth
Define number of independent runs for the target statistical uncertainty
Specify file format, naming convention, and storage estimate
Design a real-time monitoring display for key diagnostics
Define abort criteria and recovery procedures

steps.description: Fit a physical model to the data, assess goodness of fit, analyze residuals for systematic patterns, and extract the quantity of interest with its uncertainty.

outputs.name: fit-results
outputs.desc: Best-fit parameters with uncertainties and covariance matrix

outputs.name: residual-analysis
outputs.desc: Residual plots, autocorrelation, and systematic pattern flags

outputs.name: extracted-value
outputs.desc: The measured physical quantity with combined uncertainty

process: Perform a weighted least-squares or maximum likelihood fit
Report parameter values, uncertainties, and chi-squared / degrees of freedom
Plot residuals and test for autocorrelation or systematic trends
Extract the quantity of interest and propagate fit uncertainty
Compare the measured value to the theoretical prediction

description: Conduct a geological field survey: select sites, collect and log cores, identify minerals, run geochemical analyses, map formations, and reconstruct geological history.

steps.description: Select field sites based on geological maps, remote sensing data, research objectives, and access logistics.

inputs.name: regional-geology
inputs.desc: Existing maps, reports, and remote sensing imagery

outputs.name: site-list
outputs.desc: Ranked candidate sites with coordinates, access notes, and expected formations

outputs.name: logistics-plan
outputs.desc: Access routes, permits, equipment transport, and field schedule

outputs.name: sampling-targets
outputs.desc: Which formations, contacts, or features to sample at each site

process: Review existing geological maps and satellite imagery
Identify exposures, contacts, and features relevant to the research question
Rank sites by scientific value, accessibility, and safety
Plan access logistics and permitting

steps.description: Design and execute a core sampling program: drill locations, core diameter, depth targets, preservation, and logging procedures.

outputs.name: core-log
outputs.desc: Lithologic description, depth intervals, contacts, and features for each core

outputs.name: sample-inventory
outputs.desc: Labeled samples with depth, formation, and intended analysis

outputs.name: core-photos
outputs.desc: Annotated core photographs with scale bars

process: Position drill holes to intersect target formations
Core at specified diameter and depth with continuous recovery logging
Log lithology, color, grain size, fossils, and structural features per interval
Photograph cores with scale and orientation marks
Package and label samples for transport to the lab

steps.description: Identify minerals in hand samples and thin sections using optical properties, crystal form, hardness, and confirmatory tests.

inputs.name: sample-inventory
inputs.desc: Rock and mineral samples to identify

outputs.name: mineral-id-table
outputs.desc: Identified minerals per sample with diagnostic properties

outputs.name: thin-section-descriptions
outputs.desc: Petrographic descriptions of texture, mineralogy, and alteration

outputs.name: rock-classification
outputs.desc: Rock type and name per sample using IUGS or appropriate scheme

process: Examine hand samples for color, luster, streak, hardness, and crystal form
Prepare thin sections and examine under polarized light
Record mineral assemblage, texture, and modal proportions
Classify rocks using standard schemes (IUGS igneous, sedimentary grain-size, metamorphic grade)

steps.description: Plan geochemical analyses for selected samples: choose methods (XRF, ICP-MS, isotope ratios), define elements of interest, and set QA/QC procedures.

inputs.name: mineral-id-table
inputs.desc: Minerals present to guide element selection

outputs.name: geochemical-protocol
outputs.desc: Methods, elements, detection limits, and sample prep per batch

outputs.name: qaqc-plan
outputs.desc: Blanks, standards, duplicates, and acceptance criteria

outputs.name: element-suite
outputs.desc: Target analytes with expected ranges

process: Select analytical methods matched to target elements and detection limits
Define sample preparation (crushing, dissolution, fusion) per method
Design QA/QC with blanks, certified reference materials, and field duplicates
Set acceptance criteria for precision and accuracy

steps.description: Produce a geological map from field observations: plot contacts, faults, fold axes, and sample locations on a topographic base.

inputs.name: core-log
inputs.desc: Subsurface data to project to the map

inputs.name: rock-classification
inputs.desc: Rock types to map as units

outputs.name: geological-map
outputs.desc: Map with formation boundaries, structural symbols, sample locations, and cross-section lines

outputs.name: cross-sections
outputs.desc: Vertical profiles showing subsurface structure

outputs.name: structural-data-table
outputs.desc: Strike, dip, and structural measurements with locations

process: Plot field stations, contacts, and structural measurements on the base map
Trace formation boundaries between observation points
Add fault traces, fold axes, and unconformities
Draw cross-sections to show subsurface geometry
Add legend, scale, and coordinate grid

steps.description: Reconstruct the geological history of the study area from the map, stratigraphy, geochemistry, and structural data.

outputs.name: geological-history
outputs.desc: Time-ordered sequence of events (deposition, intrusion, deformation, erosion)

outputs.name: tectonic-interpretation
outputs.desc: Regional tectonic setting and its influence on local geology

outputs.name: open-questions
outputs.desc: Remaining uncertainties and further work needed

process: Apply superposition, cross-cutting, and inclusion principles to order events
Interpret depositional environments from sedimentary structures and fossils
Infer metamorphic and igneous conditions from mineral assemblages and geochemistry
Place the sequence in a regional tectonic framework
Identify remaining gaps and propose follow-up investigations

description: Characterize a new material: prepare samples, run crystallographic and microstructural analysis, test mechanical and thermal properties, measure electrical behavior, and compile a comparison report.

steps.description: Prepare samples for characterization: cutting, mounting, polishing, coating, and sectioning matched to each downstream technique.

inputs.name: material-description
inputs.desc: Composition, form (bulk, film, powder), and handling precautions

inputs.name: techniques-planned
inputs.desc: Which characterization methods will be used

outputs.name: sample-inventory
outputs.desc: Labeled samples with dimensions, preparation method, and target technique

outputs.name: preparation-log
outputs.desc: Step-by-step prep record (grinding grits, polishing compounds, etchants, coatings)

outputs.name: storage-conditions
outputs.desc: Temperature, atmosphere, and shelf-life constraints per sample

process: Section the material into specimens sized for each technique
Mount, grind, and polish metallographic samples to the required finish
Apply conductive coatings for electron microscopy samples
Prepare powder specimens for XRD (grinding, sieving, mounting)
Label and store all samples under appropriate conditions

steps.description: Run X-ray diffraction on prepared samples: collect diffractograms, identify phases, refine lattice parameters, and assess crystallinity.

inputs.name: sample-inventory
inputs.desc: Powder or thin-film samples prepared for XRD

outputs.name: xrd-results
outputs.desc: Phase IDs, lattice parameters, crystallite size, and strain estimates

outputs.name: diffractograms
outputs.desc: Annotated diffraction patterns with peak assignments

outputs.name: phase-fractions
outputs.desc: Quantitative phase analysis results if multiphase

process: Collect diffractograms at appropriate scan rate and angular range
Match peaks to reference patterns (ICDD database) for phase identification
Refine lattice parameters using Rietveld or Le Bail methods
Estimate crystallite size and microstrain from peak broadening

steps.description: Image microstructure with SEM and TEM: capture secondary and backscatter images, run EDS for composition, and measure grain sizes.

inputs.name: sample-inventory
inputs.desc: Polished and coated samples for electron microscopy

inputs.name: xrd-results
inputs.desc: Known phases to locate and confirm in images

outputs.name: microstructure-images
outputs.desc: Annotated SEM and TEM micrographs at multiple magnifications

outputs.name: eds-composition-maps
outputs.desc: Elemental distribution maps and spot analysis results

outputs.name: grain-size-distribution
outputs.desc: Measured grain size statistics (mean, standard deviation, histogram)

process: Image at low magnification for overview, then at high magnification for features
Collect secondary electron images for topography and backscatter for composition contrast
Run EDS point analysis and mapping on regions of interest
Measure grain sizes using intercept or area methods on calibrated images

steps.description: Plan and execute mechanical testing: tensile, hardness, impact, or fatigue tests matched to the application requirements.

outputs.name: mechanical-results
outputs.desc: Yield strength, UTS, elongation, hardness, and modulus with uncertainties

outputs.name: stress-strain-curves
outputs.desc: Recorded curves with labeled features (yield point, necking, fracture)

outputs.name: fracture-analysis
outputs.desc: Fracture surface description (ductile, brittle, mixed) from visual and SEM examination

process: Select test types based on application (tensile, compression, hardness, impact)
Machine specimens to standard dimensions (ASTM or ISO)
Run tests at controlled strain rate and temperature
Record and process stress-strain data, hardness indents, and impact energies
Examine fracture surfaces for failure mode

steps.description: Run thermal analysis (DSC, TGA, DMA) to identify phase transitions, decomposition temperatures, and thermal stability windows.

inputs.name: xrd-results
inputs.desc: Phases present that may undergo transitions

outputs.name: thermal-results
outputs.desc: Transition temperatures, enthalpies, mass loss steps, and glass transition data

outputs.name: thermal-curves
outputs.desc: Annotated DSC, TGA, and DMA curves

outputs.name: stability-window
outputs.desc: Safe operating temperature range with degradation onset

process: Select techniques based on expected behavior (DSC for transitions, TGA for decomposition, DMA for viscoelastic)
Set heating rate, atmosphere, and temperature range
Run samples and reference/baseline in parallel
Identify transition onsets, peaks, and mass loss steps from the curves

steps.description: Compile all characterization results into a comparison report benchmarked against published data for similar materials.

outputs.name: property-comparison-table
outputs.desc: Side-by-side comparison of measured vs published properties

outputs.name: characterization-summary
outputs.desc: One-page summary of the material's key properties and suitability

outputs.name: recommended-applications
outputs.desc: Applications where the material's properties are a good match

process: Tabulate all measured properties with uncertainties
Retrieve published data for comparable materials
Identify where the new material outperforms, matches, or falls short
Recommend applications based on the property profile

description: Design a neuroscience study: refine the research question, build the behavioral paradigm, plan neuroimaging acquisition, screen participants, preprocess data, run statistical mapping, and prepare results figures.

steps.description: Refine a neuroscience research question into a testable hypothesis with specified brain regions, cognitive processes, and expected contrasts.

inputs.name: research-question
inputs.desc: The broad neuroscience question to investigate

inputs.name: prior-findings
inputs.desc: Relevant imaging and behavioral results from the literature

outputs.name: refined-hypothesis
outputs.desc: Testable hypothesis with specific brain regions, direction of effect, and contrast of interest

outputs.name: roi-list
outputs.desc: A priori regions of interest with anatomical definitions

outputs.name: cognitive-model
outputs.desc: Diagram of the cognitive process and where the manipulation intervenes

process: Narrow the question to a specific cognitive process and its neural substrate
State the hypothesis in terms of expected activation or connectivity changes
Define regions of interest from anatomical atlases or prior coordinates
Diagram the cognitive model showing where the experimental manipulation acts

steps.description: Design the behavioral task (stimulus timing, conditions, trial structure, response recording) compatible with the imaging environment.

inputs.name: refined-hypothesis
inputs.desc: What the task needs to test

inputs.name: cognitive-model
inputs.desc: Which processes to engage or contrast

outputs.name: paradigm-spec
outputs.desc: Trial structure, timing, conditions, stimuli, and response requirements

outputs.name: stimulus-set
outputs.desc: Stimulus materials with counterbalancing scheme

outputs.name: behavioral-predictions
outputs.desc: Expected RT and accuracy differences between conditions

process: Design conditions that isolate the cognitive contrast of interest
Set trial timing compatible with the hemodynamic response (for fMRI) or ERP windowing (for EEG)
Build the stimulus set with counterbalancing across participants
Define response collection (button box, verbal, eye tracking)

steps.description: Specify the neuroimaging acquisition: modality (fMRI, EEG, or both), sequence parameters, electrode layout, session structure, and quality assurance checks.

inputs.name: roi-list
inputs.desc: Regions that determine spatial resolution and coverage needs

outputs.name: acquisition-protocol
outputs.desc: Sequence parameters (TR, TE, voxel size, slices) or EEG montage and sampling rate

outputs.name: session-structure
outputs.desc: Order of runs, rest periods, anatomical scans, and total time

outputs.name: qa-checklist
outputs.desc: Pre-scan checks (coil, motion straps, impedances) and real-time quality monitors

process: Choose imaging modality and justify based on temporal vs spatial resolution needs
Set acquisition parameters to cover ROIs at required resolution
Structure the session with task runs, rest, and anatomical acquisitions
Define real-time QA checks (motion, signal dropout, impedance)

steps.description: Design the participant screening: inclusion and exclusion criteria, informed consent, MRI safety screening, and demographic data collection.

inputs.name: acquisition-protocol
inputs.desc: Imaging modality determines safety screening requirements

outputs.name: screening-form
outputs.desc: Inclusion/exclusion criteria, MRI safety questionnaire, and demographic survey

outputs.name: consent-template
outputs.desc: Informed consent document with study description, risks, and data handling

outputs.name: target-sample-size
outputs.desc: Required N with power analysis justification

process: Define inclusion criteria (age, handedness, vision, language)
Set exclusion criteria (MRI contraindications, neurological history, medications)
Write informed consent covering procedures, risks, and data storage
Calculate target sample size from expected effect size and desired power

steps.description: Preprocess neuroimaging data: format conversion, motion correction, spatial normalization, smoothing (fMRI) or artifact rejection and re-referencing (EEG).

inputs.name: acquisition-protocol
inputs.desc: Modality and parameters determine preprocessing steps

inputs.name: session-structure
inputs.desc: Which runs to process and in what order

outputs.name: preprocessed-dataset
outputs.desc: Clean, normalized data ready for statistical analysis

outputs.name: quality-report
outputs.desc: Motion parameters, artifact counts, excluded volumes or epochs, and signal-to-noise estimates

outputs.name: preprocessing-log
outputs.desc: Software versions, parameter settings, and processing order for reproducibility

process: Convert raw data to standard format (BIDS for fMRI, EDF/BrainVision for EEG)
Apply motion correction or artifact rejection and interpolation
Normalize to standard space (MNI) or re-reference and filter (EEG)
Apply spatial smoothing or time-frequency decomposition as appropriate
Generate quality reports and flag participants for exclusion

steps.description: Run statistical analyses on preprocessed neuroimaging data: model specification, contrast estimation, multiple comparison correction, and ROI extraction.

inputs.name: roi-list
inputs.desc: A priori regions for targeted analysis

outputs.name: statistical-maps
outputs.desc: Whole-brain activation maps with corrected thresholds

outputs.name: roi-results
outputs.desc: Effect sizes and p-values within each ROI

outputs.name: results-table
outputs.desc: Peak coordinates, cluster sizes, and statistics for significant activations

process: Specify the general linear model with task regressors and confounds
Estimate contrasts of interest at the individual and group level
Apply multiple comparison correction (FWE, FDR, or cluster-based)
Extract ROI statistics and compute effect sizes
Compile a results table with MNI coordinates and cluster information

description: Run an ecological population study: design sampling, execute mark-recapture, model population dynamics, assess habitat quality, map species interactions, evaluate conservation status, and write management recommendations.

steps.description: Design a sampling scheme for population estimation: choose method (transects, quadrats, point counts, traps), set spatial layout, and determine replication.

inputs.name: target-species
inputs.desc: Species or species group to study

inputs.name: study-area
inputs.desc: Geographic extent, habitat types, and access

outputs.name: sampling-design
outputs.desc: Method, spatial layout (transect routes, plot coordinates), replication, and seasonal timing

outputs.name: detection-model
outputs.desc: Expected detection probability and factors affecting it

outputs.name: effort-schedule
outputs.desc: Number of visits, time per visit, and seasonal windows

process: Select a sampling method suited to the species' ecology and detectability
Lay out sampling units to cover habitat variation and minimize spatial bias
Estimate detection probability from pilot data or published values
Set replication to achieve the target precision for population estimates

steps.description: Design and execute a mark-recapture study: marking method, capture occasions, data recording, and assumptions to verify.

outputs.name: capture-history-matrix
outputs.desc: Binary matrix of individual detection across occasions

outputs.name: marking-protocol
outputs.desc: Mark type, application method, and individual identification scheme

outputs.name: assumption-checks
outputs.desc: Tests for equal catchability, mark loss, and closure

process: Choose a marking method that does not alter survival or behavior
Define capture occasions with sufficient intervals for mixing
Record individual captures in a standard encounter history format
Test closure and equal catchability assumptions

steps.description: Estimate population size, survival, and recruitment from capture histories using appropriate models (Lincoln-Petersen, Jolly-Seber, occupancy).

outputs.name: population-estimate
outputs.desc: Abundance estimate with confidence interval

outputs.name: demographic-rates
outputs.desc: Survival, recruitment, and growth rate estimates

outputs.name: model-selection-table
outputs.desc: Candidate models ranked by AIC or similar criterion

process: Fit candidate population models to the encounter histories
Compare models using information criteria
Extract population size, survival, and recruitment from the best model
Report estimates with confidence intervals and model-averaged values if warranted

steps.description: Map species interactions at the study site: predator-prey, competition, mutualism, and parasitism from observation, diet analysis, or network metrics.

outputs.name: interaction-network
outputs.desc: Species interaction graph with edge types (predation, competition, mutualism)

outputs.name: network-metrics
outputs.desc: Connectance, nestedness, modularity, and keystone indices

outputs.name: interaction-evidence
outputs.desc: Supporting data (diet contents, behavioral observations, co-occurrence patterns)

process: Record direct interactions from behavioral observations
Analyze diet contents or stable isotopes for trophic links
Calculate co-occurrence patterns and test against null models
Build the interaction network and compute graph metrics

steps.description: Evaluate the conservation status of the study population against IUCN criteria: population size, trend, range, threats, and viability.

outputs.name: conservation-assessment
outputs.desc: Status evaluation against IUCN criteria (A through E)

outputs.name: threat-register
outputs.desc: Ranked threats with severity, scope, and reversibility

outputs.name: viability-outlook
outputs.desc: Population viability projection under current conditions

process: Apply IUCN criterion A (population decline) from trend data
Apply criterion B (geographic range) from occurrence records
Apply criterion C (small population) from abundance estimate
Identify and rank threats by severity and scope
Project population trajectory under current threat levels

steps.description: Write management recommendations based on population status, threats, and habitat condition, with actions prioritized by feasibility and expected benefit.

outputs.name: management-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized actions with expected outcomes, timelines, and costs

outputs.name: monitoring-protocol
outputs.desc: Indicators to track and evaluation schedule

outputs.name: stakeholder-brief
outputs.desc: Non-technical summary for land managers and funders

process: Match each threat to a management action (habitat restoration, harvest regulation, invasive control)
Prioritize actions by benefit-to-cost ratio and feasibility
Define success indicators and a monitoring schedule
Write a stakeholder brief summarizing the case and recommended actions

description: Design a clinical study: formulate the PICO question, select endpoints, calculate sample size, plan randomization and blinding, set up data safety monitoring, and write the statistical analysis plan.

steps.description: Formulate a clinical research question in PICO format: population, intervention, comparator, and outcome, with inclusion and exclusion criteria.

inputs.name: clinical-question
inputs.desc: The clinical problem or treatment to investigate

outputs.name: pico-statement
outputs.desc: Structured PICO question with defined terms

outputs.name: eligibility-criteria
outputs.desc: Inclusion and exclusion criteria for enrollment

outputs.name: study-type-recommendation
outputs.desc: Recommended design (RCT, cohort, case-control) with justification

process: Define the population with specific demographic and clinical characteristics
Specify the intervention (dose, route, duration, frequency)
Choose the comparator (placebo, active control, usual care)
Define the primary outcome with its measurement method and clinically meaningful difference

steps.description: Select primary and secondary endpoints: clinical relevance, measurement validity, expected effect size, and regulatory acceptability.

inputs.name: pico-statement
inputs.desc: The research question with defined outcome

inputs.name: prior-evidence
inputs.desc: Effect sizes observed in previous trials

outputs.name: endpoint-definitions
outputs.desc: Primary and secondary endpoints with measurement method, timing, and minimally important difference

outputs.name: endpoint-justification
outputs.desc: Clinical relevance, regulatory precedent, and psychometric properties per endpoint

outputs.name: assessment-schedule
outputs.desc: When each endpoint is measured during the study

process: Select the primary endpoint based on clinical relevance and regulatory guidance
Choose secondary endpoints that capture additional dimensions of efficacy and safety
Define the measurement method, instrument, and scoring for each
Set the minimally clinically important difference for the primary endpoint

steps.description: Calculate the required sample size from the expected effect, variability, desired power, alpha level, and anticipated dropout rate.

inputs.name: prior-evidence
inputs.desc: Expected effect size and variability from pilot or prior data

outputs.name: sample-size-report
outputs.desc: Required N per arm and total, with power, alpha, effect size, and dropout adjustment

outputs.name: sensitivity-analysis
outputs.desc: How sample size changes under different assumptions about effect size and dropout

outputs.name: enrollment-timeline
outputs.desc: Expected accrual rate and time to reach target enrollment

process: Specify the test statistic matched to the endpoint type (t-test, chi-square, log-rank, mixed model)
Set alpha, power, and the clinically meaningful effect size
Calculate raw N using the appropriate formula or simulation
Inflate for expected dropout and non-compliance
Run sensitivity analyses across a range of effect sizes

steps.description: Design the randomization and blinding scheme: allocation method, stratification factors, concealment mechanism, and unblinding procedures.

outputs.name: randomization-scheme
outputs.desc: Method (simple, block, stratified, adaptive), block sizes, and stratification factors

outputs.name: blinding-protocol
outputs.desc: Who is blinded (participant, investigator, assessor), matching method, and supply logistics

outputs.name: unblinding-procedure
outputs.desc: When and how to unblind (emergency, interim, final)

process: Choose the randomization method based on study size and stratification needs
Set block sizes and stratification factors to balance arms
Design the blinding mechanism (matching placebo, coded supplies, central dispensing)
Define emergency unblinding procedures and the code custodian role

steps.description: Design the data safety monitoring framework: DSMB charter, stopping rules, interim analysis schedule, and adverse event reporting.

inputs.name: endpoint-definitions
inputs.desc: Safety and efficacy endpoints to monitor

inputs.name: sample-size-report
inputs.desc: Enrollment timeline for scheduling interim looks

outputs.name: dsmb-charter
outputs.desc: Board composition, meeting schedule, voting procedures, and confidentiality rules

outputs.name: stopping-rules
outputs.desc: Statistical boundaries for efficacy, futility, and safety (O'Brien-Fleming, Lan-DeMets, etc.)

outputs.name: adverse-event-protocol
outputs.desc: Grading scale, reporting timelines, and causality assessment method

process: Define the DSMB membership (clinicians, statistician, ethicist) and meeting schedule
Set interim analysis time points based on enrollment milestones
Choose alpha-spending function and calculate stopping boundaries
Define adverse event grading, reporting timelines, and the causality assessment method

steps.description: Write the statistical analysis plan: analysis populations, primary analysis method, sensitivity analyses, subgroup analyses, and missing data handling.

inputs.name: endpoint-definitions
inputs.desc: All endpoints and their measurement properties

outputs.name: sap-document
outputs.desc: Full statistical analysis plan with analysis populations, methods, and decision rules

outputs.name: mock-tables
outputs.desc: Shell tables and figures showing the planned layout of results

outputs.name: missing-data-strategy
outputs.desc: Approach to missing data (multiple imputation, mixed models, sensitivity analyses)

process: Define analysis populations (ITT, per-protocol, safety)
Specify the primary analysis model and its assumptions
Plan sensitivity analyses for departures from assumptions
Define subgroup analyses with multiplicity adjustment
Describe the missing data handling strategy and its justification

description: Plan and reduce astronomical observations: select targets, calculate exposures, schedule the run, reduce raw images, extract photometry or spectra, calibrate, and build the results catalog.

steps.description: Select observation targets based on scientific goals, visibility, brightness, and sky conditions.

inputs.name: science-goals
inputs.desc: What to measure or detect (transits, spectra, variability, astrometry)

inputs.name: telescope-specs
inputs.desc: Aperture, instruments available, site latitude, and typical seeing

outputs.name: target-list
outputs.desc: Targets with coordinates, magnitudes, spectral types, and priority ranking

outputs.name: visibility-windows
outputs.desc: Observable dates, hour angles, and airmass constraints per target

outputs.name: finder-charts
outputs.desc: Star charts centered on each target with comparison stars marked

process: Query catalogs (Simbad, VizieR, MAST) for candidate targets matching science criteria
Filter by magnitude limits, declination, and crowding
Compute visibility for each target across the observing season
Rank by priority and prepare finder charts with comparison and check stars

steps.description: Calculate exposure times for each target and filter combination to reach the required signal-to-noise ratio.

inputs.name: telescope-specs
inputs.desc: Aperture, detector QE, read noise, dark current, plate scale

outputs.name: exposure-plan
outputs.desc: Exposure time, number of frames, and filter for each target

outputs.name: snr-estimates
outputs.desc: Expected S/N per target under nominal conditions

outputs.name: overhead-estimate
outputs.desc: Total time including readout, slewing, and calibration frames

process: Model the source signal from magnitude, filter bandpass, and telescope throughput
Model noise sources (sky background, read noise, dark current, scintillation)
Solve for exposure time to reach target S/N
Determine number of sub-exposures to avoid saturation or trailing
Sum science time plus overheads for the full schedule

steps.description: Build the observing run schedule: order targets by hour angle, insert calibration frames, and plan for weather contingencies.

outputs.name: night-schedule
outputs.desc: Minute-by-minute schedule for each night with targets, calibrations, and contingencies

outputs.name: calibration-plan
outputs.desc: Bias, flat, dark, and standard star schedule

outputs.name: backup-targets
outputs.desc: Lower-priority targets for poor conditions or early completion

process: Order targets to minimize slew time and stay near the meridian
Insert flat fields at twilight and biases and darks at start and end
Schedule photometric or spectrophotometric standards throughout the night
Add backup targets for weather losses or schedule gaps

steps.description: Reduce raw CCD images: subtract bias, apply flat field, remove cosmic rays, align frames, and co-add for each target and filter.

inputs.name: calibration-plan
inputs.desc: Bias, flat, and dark frames collected

outputs.name: reduced-images
outputs.desc: Calibrated, cosmic-ray-cleaned, aligned, and co-added images per target and filter

outputs.name: reduction-log
outputs.desc: Processing steps, software versions, and quality metrics per frame

outputs.name: rejection-list
outputs.desc: Frames rejected for trailing, clouds, or abnormal background

process: Build master bias, dark, and flat from calibration frames
Subtract bias and dark, divide by flat for each science frame
Detect and interpolate over cosmic rays
Align frames using field stars and co-add with sigma clipping
Inspect reduced images and reject any with artifacts

steps.description: Extract photometry (aperture or PSF) or spectra (trace, extract, wavelength calibrate) from reduced images.

outputs.name: raw-measurements
outputs.desc: Instrumental magnitudes or extracted spectra with error estimates

outputs.name: extraction-diagnostics
outputs.desc: PSF fits, aperture curves of growth, or trace profiles for quality assessment

outputs.name: comparison-star-data
outputs.desc: Measurements of comparison and check stars for differential photometry

process: Detect sources and centroid on the target and comparison stars
Perform aperture photometry at multiple radii or fit a PSF model
For spectra: trace the order, extract with optimal extraction, and wavelength calibrate from arc lamps
Record instrumental measurements with Poisson and background error propagation

steps.description: Calibrate measurements to a standard system (magnitudes, flux, wavelength) and compile the final results catalog.

inputs.name: comparison-star-data
inputs.desc: Standard star measurements for zero-point and color terms

outputs.name: calibrated-catalog
outputs.desc: Final photometry or spectra on a standard system with errors

outputs.name: calibration-coefficients
outputs.desc: Zero points, color terms, extinction coefficients, and residuals

outputs.name: results-summary
outputs.desc: Key findings: variability detected, new magnitudes, spectral classifications, or transits confirmed

process: Fit transformation equations from standard star observations
Apply atmospheric extinction correction
Transform instrumental magnitudes or wavelengths to the standard system
Compile the catalog with calibrated values, errors, and flags
Summarize the scientific results and compare to predictions
